newsitem.title: USA: Invitro says will not meet profit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Invitro says will not meet profit forecast.

text.p: InVitro International said on Wednesday it will not be able to meet a company goal of being profitable in the first quarter of fiscal 1997, ending December 31.
In a statement, InVitro said the delay in obtaining the profit goal stems from its difficulty predicting how successfully its new child safety system, Guardian DNA, will be in the market.
The first shipment of redeemable Guardian brochures were sent to hospitals in December, and the product fulfillment center is ready to begin processing orders, the company said.
InVitro said it has teamed with GiftPax/American Sampling Inc to provide roughly 3.7 million new mothers during 1997 with information about Guardian DNA.

"We feel extremely confident Guardian DNA will be a success as it reaches hundreds of thousand of new mothers in January, and each successive month throughout 1997," said Richard Ulmer, chief executive officer.
"We estimate that a mere one percent response rate over the course of the next 12 months will turn the corner for the company financially," he added.

Earlier, the company reported a net loss of $0.15 a share on revenue of 1.06 million for the fiscal year ended Sept. 30, 1996 versus a net loss of $0.23 a share on revenue of $1.13 million one year before.
The company said its narrowed loss in fiscal 1996 was attributable to cost controls implemented at the company.
